description: The Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on NOAA-21 (JPSS-2, J2): 22 bands (M1-M16 with M16A/M16B, I1-I5, Day/Night Band low- and mid-gain stages) from 0.41 to 12.5 um. The curves are the VIIRS Data Analysis Working Group (DAWG) at-launch band-averaged relative spectral responses, V2 (Jul 2019), the 'Final prelaunch version' published by NOAA NCC, used to populate the VIIRS SDR look-up tables.
facility_description: The Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) is NOAA's series of polar-orbiting weather satellites (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20/J1, NOAA-21/J2, ...); VIIRS is its visible/infrared imager.

notes: V2 adds August 2016 GLAMR measurements for VisNIR and SWIR bands to the 2017 SpMA measurements; M11, M12, M14-M16 and I4-I5 are the V1 RSR repeated (README). Small negative out-of-band responses in the Fused M1-M4, M10 and I1 band averages (minimum -1.3E-3, I1) were set to 0. No J2-specific prelaunch calibration paper was verified in this pass. Curves are the DAWG band-average files; README quotes: 'The RSR are stitched IB+OOB RSR with all RSR normalized at the peak of 1.0' and low-quality response 'is set to 1E-10 in the band average RSR'. Some V1-derived file headers label the wavelength column 'wvl_um' although the values are nm (verified: each band's peak lies inside its NOAA specification spectral range). 'RSR are provided for M16A, M16B and an average of M16A and M16B referred to as M16 ... VIIRS on-orbit M16 SDR radiances consist of a time delay integration of M16A and M16B observations' (README). DNBLGS/DNBMGS are the Day/Night Band low- and mid-gain stages. Photon/energy weighting is not stated by the owner; the staged DetectorType=energy is tagged 'assumed'. Pivot check: NOAA publishes spectral ranges, not central wavelengths (NOAA-20 VIIRS On-orbit Performance table, https://ncc.nesdis.noaa.gov/NOAA-20/docs/NOAA-20-VIIRS-on-OrbitPerformanceTable.pdf); every M/I band pivot lies inside its range. Facility/instrument IDs follow SVO's JPSS/VIIRS-J1 and JPSS/VIIRS-J2 (no SVO record was available locally to confirm the mapping; the J1/J2 suffixes are NOAA's own flight designations). Instrument paper cited is the Suomi NPP VIIRS on-orbit performance paper (same instrument design).
